sections.heading: D — Accuracy
sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy

Every fact block in parts C and C-two of this section cites exactly one physical page of the registered snapshot by anchor, and the statement is paraphrased from that page alone; downshifting, parking placement and hill parking resolve to the first selected page, angle and parallel parking to the second, parking restrictions, signal types and hazard signals to the third, stop signals, turn signal rules and the start of the traffic mix to the fourth, the rest of the traffic mix, rain and hydroplaning to the fifth, and hydroplaning prevention, wet brakes, floods, fog and winter to the sixth.

Confidence: high across the section; every rule is printed directly on its page. One wording caution recorded as printed: the hill-parking page says both to turn the front wheels toward the curb and, whether uphill or downhill, to turn them to the right, and both statements are kept exactly as the page prints them without reconciling them. The hill-parking diagram labels are stated by their printed captions only.

Known source hazard: the manual's text layer carries a superseded hidden layer on some pages; every statement here was checked against the visible rendered page, not the hidden text, and no claim rests on hidden lines.

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the downshifting limits, parking placement, parking on a hill, angle and parallel parking, parking restrictions, electric and hand signals, hazard and stop signals, turn signal rules and errors, sharing the road with vehicles of all sizes, and driving in rain, hydroplaning, wet brakes, floods, fog and winter conditions rules on pages 71–76 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
